checks.title: Implicit rejection, ML-KEM-512 (Impl B + Impl C)
checks.hypothesis: A random invalid ciphertext decapsulates to a 32-byte secret that is not the valid secret, with no error (FIPS 203 §7.3).

checks.title: Implicit rejection, ML-KEM-768 (Impl A + B + C)
checks.hypothesis: A random invalid ciphertext decapsulates to a 32-byte secret that is not the valid secret, with no error, in all three implementations.

checks.title: Implicit rejection, ML-KEM-1024 (Impl A + B + C)
checks.hypothesis: A random invalid ciphertext decapsulates to a 32-byte secret that is not the valid secret, with no error, in all three implementations.

checks.title: Implicit rejection is deterministic (J(z || c))
checks.hypothesis: Decapsulating the same invalid ciphertext twice returns the identical pseudorandom secret (FIPS 203 §7.3: K = J(z || c)).

checks.title: All-zero ciphertext is implicitly rejected
checks.hypothesis: An all-zero ciphertext decapsulates to a 32-byte secret different from the valid secret, with no error.

checks.title: Single-bit-flipped valid ciphertext is implicitly rejected
checks.hypothesis: Flipping one bit of a valid ciphertext makes decapsulation return a different 32-byte secret with no error (re-encryption mismatch).

checks.title: Ciphertext from another keypair is implicitly rejected
checks.hypothesis: A valid ciphertext under Alice's key decapsulated with Bob's key returns a 32-byte secret different from both parties' valid secrets.

checks.title: No oracle signal: valid vs invalid decapsulation outputs
checks.hypothesis: Valid and invalid decapsulation are indistinguishable by return type, return length, and exception behaviour — no error signal leaks the validity of a ciphertext (timing not measured; see FINDINGS.md).

checks.title: Malformed-length inputs are rejected at the API boundary
checks.hypothesis: Truncated, empty, and oversized ciphertexts and decapsulation keys are rejected with an error (never a secret) by every implementation's checked entry point (FIPS 203 §7.2/§7.3 input validation).

checks.title: Wycheproof decapsulation cases, all parameter sets
checks.hypothesis: Impl C passes every Wycheproof ML-KEM decapsulation case: valid cases return K, malformed-length cases are rejected.

checks.title: CCTV strcmp + malleable-ciphertext trap cases
checks.hypothesis: The comparison in decapsulation covers the full ciphertext: the CCTV strcmp trap (difference hidden after a NUL byte) and the malleable-ciphertext cases (modification at byte 0) all return the implicit-rejection key, never the real key.

checks.title: Wycheproof semi-expanded decapsulation cases
checks.hypothesis: Decapsulation from an expanded decapsulation key: valid cases return K; wrong-length dk or ct are rejected (FIPS 203 §7.3).

checks.title: Hybrid concat-KDF combiner failure behaviour
checks.hypothesis: A hybrid combiner built from X25519 + ML-KEM: a valid run is reproducible; an invalid ML-KEM ciphertext or a wrong classical peer key changes the hybrid secret silently (no error); malformed combiner inputs are rejected. Only key confirmation can detect the failure.

checks.title: Hybrid XOR combiner leaks component secrets
checks.hypothesis: An XOR combiner (hybrid = classical XOR ML-KEM): an invalid ML-KEM ciphertext changes the hybrid silently, and knowledge of one component recovers the other from the hybrid output.

checks.title: Pinned postfiatd tree contains no ML-KEM code
checks.hypothesis: The pinned postfiatd tree has zero ML-KEM/Kyber files: there are no ML-KEM encapsulation/decapsulation paths, ciphertext validation, or combiner logic to audit in-tree.

checks.title: CCTV unlucky-SampleNTT vectors, all parameter sets
checks.hypothesis: Impl C reproduces the CCTV 'unlucky' vectors: encapsulation of m under the file's ek gives exactly the file's K and c, and decapsulation of c under the file's dk returns K. These keys need an unusually large number of XOF reads in SampleNTT, so they exercise the sampler's stream sizing.
